periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.15872 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.33); the adopted 0.95148 d is 5.99 x that. The true period is more likely 0.15872 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.31743 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

checks: No eclipse at 109 of 110 covered epochs where the 0.95148 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.

writeup: TIC 355828577 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.9515 days. Data from NASA's TESS mission shows a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 1.40 percent, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 33.7 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level analysis confirms this signal at a peak signal-to-noise of 10.9, though with a centroid offset of 3.9 arcsec from the target location. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The automated machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.28 on a scale where higher values indicate greater confidence in the target's validity.
